en.title: Queueing for Entry to an Exclusive Event
en.description:
Guests arrive in non-decreasing order. An ID check takes 300 seconds. The guest currently being checked is not counted in the waiting queue; if, on arrival, the number of waiting guests is already greater than 10, the guest leaves and their arrival time is output. If a guest arrives at the same moment a check finishes, the guests already waiting start their check first, and the new guest joins the end of the queue. Output each guest's completion time; for guests who leave, output their arrival time.

The input protocol and the examples in this batch were compiled by CSWork.
en.input: The first line contains n (1..5000); the second line contains n non-decreasing non-negative integer arrival times (≤10^9).
en.output: Output n space-separated integers in arrival order.
en.explanation: Process according to the definite rules above; see the accompanying editorial for the approach, proof of correctness, and complexity.
hints: Maintain a queue of future completion times. Before an arrival, remove everyone already finished; the front of the queue, if any, is the guest being served, and the rest are the waiting count. If it exceeds 10, the guest leaves; otherwise they join the end of the queue.
